items.title: Three remanded over RM51,000 false claims for wedding catering
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded three individuals, including a former manager of a frozen food company, for allegedly submitting false claims amounting to RM51,000. Senior Assistant Registrar Yuhanis Mohd Roslan issued the remand order following an application by the MACC at the Kuala Terengganu magistrate's court today. The male suspect was remanded for four days until July 30, while the two female suspects were remanded for three days until July 29.

items.title: Anthony Loke slams ‘baseless’ Adat interference claims, says rivals scapegoating DAP amid royal crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — DAP secretary general Anthony Loke has denied claims that he interfered in Negeri Sembilan’s Adat Perpatih institution, describing the allegations as baseless. According to Malaysiakini , the Chennah assemblyman said rumours linking him to the ongoing royal dispute in the state were unfounded, including suggestions that he had channelled funds to a faction opposed to Sungai Ujong chieftain Mubarak Thahak. Loke said the crisis was triggered when 14 Umno assemblymen led by Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Jalaluddin Alias withdrew their support for the Harapan led state government.

items.title: Fire breaks out at hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 27 — A fire involving an estimated two-acre hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam broke out this morning, with firefighting operations currently underway. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.06 am, prompting the deployment of a team from the Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) to the scene. Ashrul Riezal said the operation involves four personnel and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) from BBP Bestari Jaya, while PBS Saujana deployed four members to assist in controlling the blaze.

items.title: Fuziah: Competition Act amendments aim to curb cartels, monopolies driving up living costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Amendments to the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712) aim to curb cartels, monopolies, and anti-competitive practices driving up the cost of living. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026 will strengthen the Malaysia Competition Commission's (MyCC) ability to counter tactics used by enterprises to evade enforcement. Fuziah said fair market competition encourages enterprises to boost efficiency, innovation, and product quality, allowing consumers to enjoy competitive prices.

items.title: SUV driver held after cops find RM6,000 in smuggled bromeliad plants
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 31-year-old motorist was arrested yesterday after General Operations Force personnel found 30 bromeliad plants worth more than RM6,000, believed to have been smuggled from Thailand, in his vehicle. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure was made during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan about 6.30pm. Radzi said the driver, the vehicle and the plants were later seized.

items.title: PM Anwar says Malaysia’s only cost for Bahrain F1 Grand Prix is RM16m Sepang track upgrades
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — Malaysia will not incur any registration fees from the International Automobile Federation (FIA) for hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang this October, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Formula 1 and the FIA yesterday confirmed that Malaysia will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, scheduled between the Azerbaijan and Singapore Grands Prix from October 2 to 4, 2026. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the only expenditure Malaysia would bear is for upgrading the Sepang track, BH reported.

items.title: Indonesia's Prabowo approval rating drops to 51.1 per cent, survey finds
items.summary: Nearly half of the respondents, or 49.4 per cent, said economic conditions were either "bad" or "very bad", with just 15.7 per cent saying the economy was doing well, down from 40 per cent in November. As many as 42.8 per cent of the respondents said Prabowo's handling of the political situation was "bad" or "very bad", up sharply from 23 per cent in November. On law enforcement, 37.6 per cent of the respondents said conditions were either "bad" or "very bad."

items.title: Simpang Ampat shooting: Witness mistook gunshots for exploding lorry tyre
items.summary: SIMPANG AMPAT: A witness initially mistook the sound of gunfire for a burst trailer lorry tyre before discovering a wounded man had run into her eatery seeking refuge. She said they did not immediately suspect the sounds were gunshots as the shop is located along a busy road frequently used by lorries, where tyre blowouts are not uncommon. "A short while later, a man suddenly ran into the shop.

items.title: Anwar says govt reviewing promotion process for senior military officers
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — The government is reviewing the promotion process for senior officers of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) to ensure their career progression is not unduly delayed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. I have asked the Chief Secretary to the Government (Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar) whether we can review the process. Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief of Defence Forces General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: Oil prices dip over 6pct after US, Iran pause fighting over weekend
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell US$6.20, or 6.4 per cent, to US$90.58 by 0620 GMT after briefly slipping under the key support level of US$90 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$83.51 a barrel, down US$5.80, or 6.5 per cent. Brent had reached US$100 per barrel as the conflict, which reduced oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, spilled over to the Red Sea, hindering exports from the world's top exporter, Saudi Arabia, via the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Asia.

items.title: New Statistics Bill aims to modernise Malaysia’s data system, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Statistics Bill 2026 is expected to be gazetted by the end of this year after completing the administrative process following its approval in Parliament, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry would conduct a stakeholder engagement process after the bill is passed to enhance understanding of the importance of the new act. Commenting on the independence of official statistics from political influence, he said the Statistics Bill 2026 strengthens governance through the establishment of the National Statistics Council, which will play a role in assessing the direction and development of the country’s statistics.

items.title: Body of Malaysian stabbed to death in South Korea to be repatriated
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a Malaysian man who died after being stabbed during a group fight in South Korea will be repatriated after the necessary documentation is completed. His sister, Ain Sephia, 25, said her sister-in-law had confirmed that an autopsy on Ahmad's body had been completed. Ahmad died after being stabbed during a group fight in South Korea.

items.title: South Korea's ex-president found guilty of election disinformation
items.summary: SEOUL: A South Korean court handed jailed ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol an 18-month suspended sentence on Monday for spreading disinformation in his 2022 election campaign before his martial law bid. The Seoul Central District Court ruling could see South Korea's main opposition People Power Party (PPP), which Yoon represented, forced to pay 39.7 billion won (US$29 million) to the election commission if it is upheld on appeal. Monday's sentence, suspended for three years, was handed down by judges who found Yoon guilty of twin violations of polling legislation by making false statements on the 2022 election trail.

items.title: Pahang agri exhibition posts RM2.3 million sales from over 200,000 visitors
items.summary: KUANTAN: The rebranded Pahang Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) in Raub concluded on a high note yesterday, recording RM2.3 million in sales and surpassing its RM1.3 million target. "MAHA Pahang has achieved a proud and outstanding feat. The event was rebranded as MAHA Pahang this year.

items.title: Johor exco confirms Network School has not appealed, business licence revoked and operations halted
items.summary: KULAI, July 27 — The local authorities have yet to receive an appeal from the Network School for the resumption of operations following the revocation of its business licence last week. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has yet to receive an appeal application from the Network School’s representative. He said that the Network School is understood to have ceased its business operations.

items.title: Man shot after buying eggs in Simpang Ampat
items.summary: SIMPANG AMPAT: A 38-year-old man with a previous criminal record was injured after he was shot outside a row of shophouses in Jalan Perniagaan Seri Tambun here today. The victim ran into a nearby eatery, but the suspect pursued him and fired several more shots, with one shot hitting the victim's right hand.The suspect fled in a car. The injured man was rushed to Seberang Jaya Hospital for treatment.

items.title: School bullying: NUTP backs appointing military veterans as full-time school wardens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) supports appointing military veterans as full-time school wardens, with an initial rollout at selected fully residential schools. Its president, Aminuddin Awang, said the Education Ministry's biggest challenge was managing nearly 1,900 boarding schools nationwide. What matters is having full-time wardens at boarding schools, especially fully residential schools.

items.title: IPCC receives 1,635 complaints against police since 2023, says Saifuddin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) has received 1,635 public complaints since it began operations in 2023 up to July 24, 2026, reflecting growing public confidence in its role as an independent police oversight body. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that of the total, 844 complaints, or 76 per cent, have been resolved, while 372 complaints were received this year as of July 24. Saifuddin Nasution said the remaining unresolved complaints include cases involving complainants who were dissatisfied with the outcome of police investigations or had not received any response after lodging their complaints with the police.

items.title: Contractor loses RM122,552 in fake polytechnic tender scam
items.summary: KUANTAN: A contractor lost RM122,552 after being tricked into making compulsory upfront payments for a non-existent polytechnic supply tender. Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the victim was contacted earlier this month by an individual claiming to be a polytechnic staff member, inviting his company to submit a quotation to supply a generator. "The victim made several payments totalling RM122,552 to a bank account provided by the suspect.

items.title: Anwar says creation of Malay reserve land in KL proves commitment to Bumiputera interests
items.summary: Anwar said that after taking office in 2022, his administration moved to address the declining amount of Malay reserve land in the capital. “Since Independence in 1957, no new Malay reserve land had been created in Kuala Lumpur. “Within the area, I designated 50 acres (20 hectares) as Malay reserve land, comprising some of the most valuable land in Kuala Lumpur,” he said.

items.title: Nga: Political leaders must unite Malaysians, not divide them
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All political leaders must uphold moderation, mutual respect and national unity, says DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming. The housing and local government minister said responsible leadership should focus on bringing Malaysians together instead of exploiting differences for political gain. "People want solutions, not division.

items.title: Anwar: Cabinet to decide Wednesday whether to release Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — The Cabinet will decide on Wednesday whether to make public the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said the issue would be deliberated at the weekly Cabinet meeting before a final decision is made on the report’s release. Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: Negri Sembilan Palace warns parties against dragging royalty into polls campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Palace has reminded political parties against dragging the royal institution into state election campaigns. Comptroller of the Royal Household Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said the royal institution remains neutral and is neither affiliated with any political party nor involved in political activities. "The royal institution serves as a unifying force for the people, safeguarding harmony, stability and the nation's well-being.

items.title: Malaysia's E&E sector gains from global supply chain shift, says UOB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's electrical and electronics (E&E) sector has emerged as one of the main beneficiaries of the global supply chain restructuring triggered by the escalation of US tariffs in April 2025. "For Malaysia, the E&E sector remains the primary channel through which these opportunities are materialising. "Rising exports, expanding participation in artificial intelligence-related supply chains, stronger re-export activity and growing Chinese investment inflows all underscore Malaysia's increasing strategic importance in regional manufacturing networks," it said.

items.title: Felda's decline caused by political interference, says Anwar
items.summary: TAMPIN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has attributed Felda's financial troubles to excessive political interference in its management. He said Felda, once regarded as the world's largest plantation organisation with annual profits running into billions of ringgit, had accumulated nearly RM10 billion in debt due to poor governance over the past several years. Anwar said the government was now allocating RM980 million annually to service Felda's losses.

items.title: Sweden's far-right leader Akesson brought fringe party to brink of power
items.summary: Jimmie! Jimmie!" "I said already in my inauguration speech as party leader in 2005 that we will become a large party with great influence over politics, that we will eventually be a government party and challenge the Social Democrats as the largest party," he said.

items.title: Azalina says October rulers’ meeting to decide on AG‑Prosecutor split, Cabinet backs reforms
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, said the decision to present the recommendations of the Special Select Committee regarding the amendment was made by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during a Cabinet meeting. Azalina said the Cabinet decision also covers recommendations on limiting the Prime Minister’s term of office. Earlier, in response to Abdul Halim’s initial question on the government’s institutional reform agenda, she said 21 major reform initiatives had been implemented from 2022 to 2025.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia needs only RM16mil for Sepang F1 preparations, says Anwar
items.summary: TAMPIN: Malaysia will only need to spend an estimated RM16 million to prepare the Sepang International Circuit for the return of Formula One, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said Bahrain had agreed to absorb the substantial upfront payment to the International Automobile Federation (FIA) after deciding to relocate its Grand Prix to Malaysia due to regional security concerns. He said the arrangement meant Malaysia would only need to carry out minor maintenance works on the Sepang circuit.

items.title: Royal diplomacy brings Bahrain F1 Grand Prix to Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Royal diplomacy between His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain's King Hamad Isa Al Khalifa has paved the way for the return of Formula One (F1) to Malaysia after an eight-year absence. The Bahrain Grand Prix will be staged at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit following discussions between the two monarchs, according to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page today. "The understanding led to an agreement to stage the Bahrain Formula 1 Grand Prix at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit, bringing Formula 1 back to Malaysia after it was last held in 2017," it said.

items.title: Anwar: Any action taken based on Tabung Haji RCI must follow due process
items.summary: TAMPIN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said whether the cabinet decides to publicly release the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Tabung Haji, whatever legal action is taken must follow due process. The prime minister said any action taken based on the RCI must also be free of political interference. "As prime minister, my responsibility is to ensure the process remains free (of political interference) and follows the Federal Constitution and the laws that have been established," he said.

items.title: Remand extended for two men in murder of 10-year-old girl
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The remand order for two men detained over the murder of a 10-year-old girl, whose body was found in Sepanggar last week, has been extended until Friday (July 31). Investigating officer Assistant Superintendent La Paula Abd Muis said the extension was granted for another week to allow police to complete investigations. The two suspects — a 39-year-old undocumented man and a 42-year-old local man — were initially remanded for seven days until July 24 before police applied for an extension.

items.title: FWCMS helps curb foreign workers abuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Worker Centralised Management System (FWCMS), developed by Bestinet Sdn Bhd, has helped curb the exploitation of foreign workers by cartels and prevent such practices from becoming more widespread in Malaysia. Senior lecturer in economics at the Department of Economics and Financial Studies of Universiti Teknologi Mara Selangor branch Dr Nurul Ainun Ahmad Atory said foreign worker cartels could have become more entrenched without FWCMS. Nurul Ainun said the previous manual system created opportunities for exploitation and abuse, whereas a centralised digital platform has helped improve governance and transparency.

items.title: Petaling Jaya Sessions Court hears pleas as six accused face RM8m ransom kidnap charges
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 27 — Six men pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to charges of abducting a businessman and demanding RM8 million in ransom at Dataran Sunway on July 16. Berita Harian (BH) reported, A Ravichandran, 45; R Elanggovan, 45; M Jeyaraj, 43; Moses De Bretto John Patrick, 40; Ziyauddin, 33; and Muhammad Afiq Safine, 36, entered their pleas after the charges were read before Judge Dr Syahliza Warnoh. He told the court that Ravichandran supports a wife working as a clerk earning RM1,800 a month and three children; Elanggovan is the sole breadwinner earning RM1,500 monthly with a wife and three children; while Jeyaraj supports a wife and two children, BH reported.

items.title: SevenCo launches RM192mil Penang affordable housing project as demand stays firm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SevenCo Prestige Sdn Bhd has launched Sevora Residence, a RM192 million freehold affordable housing development in Bukit Mertajam, Penang, as demand for value-driven homes continues to underpin the state's residential market. The project comprises 420 Rumah Mampu Milik (RMM) PN1 units priced between RM388,000 and RM489,200, targeting first-time homebuyers, young families and owner-occupiers seeking quality homes in Seberang Perai, one of Penang's fastest-growing residential and industrial corridors. Located on a 1.398-hectare site along Jalan Song Ban Kheng, the project comprises a 34-storey residential tower with 420 units and eight commercial lots.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia to suspend trading in BHIC Securities on Aug 7
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in the securities of Boustead Heavy Industries Corporation Bhd (BHIC) from 9am on Friday, Aug 7, 2026, to facilitate the implementation of the company's selective capital reduction and repayment exercise. Bursa Malaysia also advised investors to refer to BHIC's announcement dated July 24, 2026, as well as the notice to shareholders and redeemable convertible preference shareholders dated July 27, 2026, for further details. At 12.30pm, BHIC shares rose one sen to 48 sen, with 37,600 shares traded.

items.title: Palace says Sultan Ibrahim’s friendship with Bahrain king paved way for F1 race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is the result of diplomatic ties and the close friendship between the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and Bahrain’s ruler, King Hamad Isa Al Khalifa. “Since 2017, His Majesty and King Hamad have developed a good personal friendship, and this has continued to grow into a strengthening of diplomatic relations between Bahrain and Malaysia, with Sultan Ibrahim’s state visit to Bahrain in 2025. As a result, an agreement was reached to host the Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix at the Petronas SIC, where Malaysia last staged an F1 race in 2017.

items.title: RM5bil financing pool to back Malaysian startups over 18 months
items.summary: Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said the funding pool will support startups and innovators at different stages of growth, although applicants must meet the eligibility criteria set by each participating institution. "We have connected 15 organisations, including funding agencies and financial institutions. Among the participating organisations are the Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology and Innovation, MBSB Bank and EXIM Bank Malaysia.

items.title: Melaka Customs seizes RM8.36mil shark fins declared as fish skin
items.summary: MELAKA: The Customs Department has foiled an attempt to smuggle 5,069kg of shark fins worth RM8.36 million after an importing company declared the cargo as fish skin. Melaka Customs director Roslan Yusoff said the shark fins, believed to have been imported from Guyana, South America, were seized on July 2. Roslan said this at a press conference at the Melaka Customs Building in Ayer Keroh today.

items.title: Network School yet to appeal licence revocation, says Johor exco
items.summary: KULAI: The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has yet to receive an appeal from Network School following the revocation of its business licence last week. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said no appeal application had been submitted to the local authority so far. Jafni said MBIP took action after identifying two clear licensing violations committed by the company.

items.title: Far-right Australian politician loses appeal in racism case
items.summary: Senator Pauline Hanson has emerged as one of Australia's most popular politicians, wooing voters with calls for strict immigration curbs, mass deportations of "illegal migrants" and enhanced free speech protections. Hanson took aim at Pakistan-born Australian lawmaker Mehreen Faruqi in 2022 over comments made in the wake of Queen Elizabeth II's death. Hanson replied on social media: "When you immigrated to Australia you took every advantage of this country.

items.title: Socso: Four Bentong accident victims covered under Lindung 24 Jam, families to receive long‑term support
items.summary: The next of kin of each victim are also eligible to receive the Funeral Management Benefit, amounting to RM3,000, paid as a one-time sum. “The late Alaganathan’s next of kin are also eligible for the same benefit. The organisation also confirmed that the families of the late Kanabati Raja and Parathanman have been verified as eligible to receive the Dependents’ Benefit under Lindung 24 Jam, as well.

items.title: Seattle shooting suspect in custody, local media reports 2 dead, 5 injured
items.summary: SEATTLE: At least two people were killed and five others, including a 2-year-old child, were wounded on Sunday in a shooting at a downtown Seattle food festival, local news outlets reported, with the US city's mayor's office saying a suspect had been taken into custody. Shots fired at the Seattle Center," the department said on X. The Seattle Times and local TV station KOMO, citing the Seattle Fire Department, reported the death and injury toll.

items.title: Saifuddin: No let-up in Immigration action despite over-capacity depots
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry will not reduce the momentum of Immigration Department enforcement operations against foreigners who violate the Immigration Act. This is despite all 19 detention depots nationwide currently operating beyond capacity, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said enforcement must continue as it involves matters of national security and sovereignty, in addition to ensuring foreigners in Malaysia comply with the law.

items.title: Don’t link royalty to your campaigns, Negeri Sembilan Palace tells parties
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 27 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace today advised political parties against associating the palace or members of the royal family with their campaigns, stressing that the royal institution remains politically neutral. In a statement, the palace said any claim, statement, photograph, video or other material linking the Negeri Sembilan Palace, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan or any member of the royal family to a political party was untrue. “The Royal Institution has always upheld the principle of neutrality and is not involved with any political party or political activity,” it said.

items.title: Chang Lih Kang says Sanusi’s comments ‘inappropriate, hurtful’, urges sensitivity during campaigns
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 27 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang has described recent remarks by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor as inappropriate and potentially hurtful to the public, urging politicians to exercise greater sensitivity, particularly during election campaigns. Chang said political leaders should be mindful of their statements to help preserve social harmony in Malaysia. On the TechnoMART Malaysia programme, Chang said RM5 billion in financing has been made available through a collaboration involving 15 organisations, including funding agencies and financial institutions, to support startups and innovators.

items.title: Body of Malaysian man killed in South Korea stabbing to be repatriated after documentation completed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — The body of a Malaysian man who died after he was allegedly stabbed during a group fight involving foreign nationals in South Korea will be brought home once documentation is completed. Family members are currently handling the repatriation process for Ahmad Shah, 26, in Eumseong County, North Chungcheong Province, according to a report by Berita Harian. Ahmad Shah was reported to have died after he was allegedly stabbed during a large brawl in South Korea.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: Police approve 473 campaign permits, open 14 investigation papers
items.summary: Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said all approved political programmes and activities were monitored by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to ensure they complied with the law and did not jeopardise public safety or order. He said that during the same period, state police received 33 police reports and opened 14 investigation papers related to election offences. “Yesterday, police received five reports from members of the public.

items.title: Immigration raids to continue despite overcrowded detention depots, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will not scale back immigration enforcement operations against foreign nationals who violate the Immigration Act 1959/63, despite the country’s 19 immigration detention depots currently operating beyond capacity. Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said enforcement efforts must continue as they are crucial to safeguarding national security and sovereignty, while ensuring foreign nationals in Malaysia comply with the country’s laws. “Malaysia is an open country.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: 22,339 military and police personnel, spouses to cast early ballots tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 27 — A total of 16,884 military personnel and their spouses, and 5,455 police personnel and their spouses will cast their ballots in early voting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election tomorrow. Among the early polling centres are the Army Basic Training Centre (PUSASDA) in Port Dickson, the Negeri Sembilan Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK), Sendayan Air Base in Seremban and the Nilai District Police Headquarters (IPD). Parti Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia (Berjasa) has fielded seven candidates.

items.title: Malaysia must adopt integrated ‘one system, one command, one action’ for air‑disaster response, says DPM Zahid
items.summary: SEPANG, July 27 — Malaysia needs to develop an integrated air disaster management system that enables all agencies to share a common operational picture, follow unified directives, and respond simultaneously to ensure faster and more effective emergency operations. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the principle of “one system, one command, and one action” must underpin the country’s disaster management framework, allowing the assets, expertise, and authority of various agencies to be coordinated towards a common objective of saving lives and bringing emergencies under control as quickly as possible. When a crisis strikes, we must respond as one national team with a clear objective,” he said at the launch of the National Air Disaster Preparedness 2026: Air Disaster Management Workshop here today.

items.title: Economy Ministry targets RM58b development spending for 2027 despite global supply crisis
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The government aims to maintain its development spending goals for 2027, Economy Minister Akmal Nasir Nasrullah said today, even as the Anwar administration faces a global energy supply crisis that prompted some budget cuts for key ministries. Akmal told reporters after speaking at his ministry’s monthly assembly here that the projection for total development expenditure needed in 2027 would be RM58 billion, with at least 70 per cent allocated to basic development. “For development expenditure (DE), as we have fiscal space to guarantee spending on facilitating development, the space for basic development must be preserved,” he said.

items.title: Home Minister: Prisons Act amendments aim to protect prison officers, not grant them immunity
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — Amending the Prisons Act 1995 aims only protect prison officers exercising their duties within their stipulated limits, and not to grant them legal immunity, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. Saifuddin Nasution said the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) is still free to make its recommendations and stressed that the Home Ministry will not defend any officers caught flouting the rules. “However, we have to be fair when civil servants, including Prisons Department officers, face legal action even after performing their duties responsibly,” he said at the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly.

items.title: Economy Ministry must bridge gap between GDP figures and people’s lived reality, says minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — Economy Minister Akmal Nasir Nasrullah today said his ministry must address the perception “gap” between the country’s growth data and what is felt on the ground. Speaking at the ministry’s monthly assembly here, Akmal pointed to the salary-productivity relationship as a glaring example of this gap. In May, the manufacturing sector recorded a 7.7 per cent productivity growth per worker, yet salaries grew only by 1.8 per cent in the same period, Akmal revealed.

items.title: Police: Driver in Teluk Intan crash that killed two teenage girls tests positive for drugs
items.summary: IPOH, July 27 — The driver believed to have caused the crash that claimed the lives of two teenage girls on Jalan Padang Tembak, Teluk Intan yesterday evening, has tested positive for benzodiazepines. Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said an initial urine screening conducted on the 28-year-old suspect returned a positive result for the drug. The crash occurred at about 6.35pm yesterday.

items.title: MetMalaysia activates warning for storms hitting Selangor, Perak, Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia identified the affected areas as Selangor (specifically Sabak Bernam) and Perak (Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk, and Hilir Perak). A similar warning was issued for Sarawak, covering Betong, Sarikei (Pakan, Sarikei, and Meradong), Sibu (Sibu), Mukah (Tanjung Manis and Daro), Kapit, Bintulu (Tatau), Miri, and Limbang (Limbang). In Sabah, similar weather conditions are forecast for the Interior Division (Sipitang, Kuala Penyu, and Beaufort), the West Coast Division (Papar, Putatan, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran, and Kota Belud), and the Kudat Division (Kudat).

items.title: Home Minister tells Malaysians to judge government by performance, not through racial lens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today urged Malaysians to evaluate politics based on the Madani administration’s performance, and not through identity politics. Saifuddin Nasution said performance based politics aims for everyone to advance the country’s economic agenda collectively, to benefit all Malaysians regardless of their race or religion. “Identity politics is about winner versus loser, us versus them.

items.title: Home Minister tells AKPS to fast-track new uniforms, ensure competency before JB-Singapore RTS Link launch in 2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today instructed the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) to expedite the distribution of new uniforms for its officers before the JB-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link enters operation in January 2027. “Make sure the new uniforms are ready, Datuk Suhaily. We are nearing the launch of RTS,” Saifuddin Nasution told AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain during the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly today.

items.title: Nearly 2,000 dogs and cats neutered under Perak initiative since 2024
items.summary: State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said that during the same period, 1,285 dog licences were also issued through collaboration with local authorities. They reflect the state government’s continued commitment, together with local authorities, the NGO Friends of Pawsitive, veterinary clinics and volunteers, to developing a more responsible and sustainable pet management system,” she said. Meanwhile, Ng said the issue of stray animals goes beyond animal welfare, as it also affects community well-being, public safety and the management responsibilities of local authorities.

items.title: Terengganu contractor duped of RM152,550 in non-existent tender scam
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 27 — A 68-year-old electrical contractor lost RM152,550 after falling victim to a non-existent tender scam. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim received an email on July 14 offering a project to install solar lights in Kampung Tanjung Baharu, Hulu Terengganu. He said the victim, who was interested in the offer, subsequently contacted a male suspect posing as an officer from the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) via WhatsApp to obtain further information.

items.title: Two teenage girls killed after car loses control and crashes into motorcycle in Teluk Intan
items.summary: IPOH, July 27 — Two teenage girls were killed after the motorcycle they were riding was involved in a crash on Jalan Padang Tembak in Teluk Intan yesterday. Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said police received a report on the incident at about 6.35 pm. He said the car driver has been detained to assist in the investigation, adding that investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause of the crash.
